description: This case study is the Congressional Research Service report Puerto Rico: Status of Electric Power Recovery, dated 10 July 2018, on how the island's grid fared and was restored after Hurricanes Irma and Maria in September 2017. It notes that Maria made landfall as a Category 4 storm with sustained winds over 155 miles per hour after Irma had left 70% of electricity customers without power, and that the central electric system was left essentially destroyed, with the power authority's infrastructure already in poor condition. It describes the federal role in restoring power, including FEMA's supply of about 900 portable generators and its coordination with the US Army Corps of Engineers, which led the grid repair. Access: free to read on the EveryCRSReport site with no licence stated. Coverage is Puerto Rico and the 2017 hurricane season. Caveats: only the opening summary was read, and the report predates the later recovery and reconstruction phases. It suits resilience and emergency response studies of island power systems, and relates to the PR100 Puerto Rico grid resilience study catalogued here.

name: Puerto Rico: Status of Electric Power Recovery after Hurricanes Irma and Maria (Congressional Research Service report R45263, July 2018)
outcomes: The report records that Maria, a Category 4 storm, left the entire island without power after Irma had already cut power to 70% of customers, that the grid was in poor condition from underinvestment before the storms, and that FEMA supplied about 900 portable generators and coordinated restoration in which the Army Corps of Engineers took the lead.
resources_used: Public statements and data of FEMA, the US Army Corps of Engineers and Puerto Rico's emergency management office
